title: Watch it, then take it back
prompt: Release 1.5.0 is rolling out. Fill in the blanks to wait for the rollout, list the Deployment's revisions, roll back to the previous one, and roll the Helm-managed staging release back to revision 4.
hints: All three `kubectl rollout` subcommands are single words: one waits, one lists, one reverses.
Helm's command for returning to an earlier release has the same name as the concept.
explanation:
```bash
kubectl rollout status deployment/notes-api --timeout=5m
kubectl rollout history deployment/notes-api
kubectl rollout undo deployment/notes-api
helm rollback notes-api 4 -n notes
```
`status` blocks until the rollout finishes and exits non-zero if it fails, which makes it a good CI gate. `undo` scales the previous ReplicaSet back up with the same rolling-update rules. `helm rollback` re-applies all manifests from release revision 4. Afterwards, revert the change in Git so the next deploy doesn't bring 1.5.0 back.
